newsitem.title: USA: U.S. declines comment on Saudi oil-for-planes idea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. declines comment on Saudi oil-for-planes idea.

text.p: U.S. administration officials Monday declined to comment on whether Saudi Arabia was considering using oil to pay for a purchase of up to 100 Lockheed Martin Corp F-16 fighter planes.

According to a trade publication, The Oil Daily, Saudi officials led by Defense Minister Prince Sultan bin Abdul-Aziz, planned to discuss the multibillion dollar oil-for-planes idea with U.S. officials here later this month.
Two administration officials said they were "unaware of any formal proposal," but said the idea had been floated before.
U.S. officials so far have been unable to confirm whether Saudi Minister of Petroleum Ali Naimi would join Sultan for the talks in Washington, another administration source said.

The U.S. Defense Department and White House last week acknowledged that the Saudis were talking to contractors about a potential plane purchase, but said the government had received no formal request or proposal yet.
The Defense Department Monday said it had nothing more to add to last week's comments.

One administration official said several years ago the U.S. government had looked at taking oil from the kingdom to erase some Saudi debts to Washington for military purchases, but the idea was rejected.
The official said the oil would have had to go into the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. Taking the Saudi oil would have required a reversal of a U.S. policy not to fill the SPR at the time, he said.
The United States has added no oil to the SPR since 1994.
Saudi Embassy officials were not available for comment Monday.
Lockheed's tactical aircraft division in Fort Worth, Texas, declined to comment on any aspect of the negotiations with the Saudis.
